source.citation: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center. NOAA Space Weather Scales (Solar Radiation Storms, S1-S5). Web page https://www.swpc.noaa.gov/noaa-scales-explanation (served from www.spaceweather.gov) and PDF 'NOAA Space Weather Scales', dated December 11, 2023, https://www.swpc.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/images/NOAAscales.pdf. Accessed 2026-11-14.

caveats: Thresholds are NOAA's operational definition: >=10 MeV integral proton flux, 5-minute averages, pfu = particles cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1. LANDFALL triggers on this scale and does not project its own mSv.

NOAA's 'Biological' text is written for astronauts on EVA and for high-latitude aircraft crews; it is not a NASA crew-health limit and carries no NASA requirement ID. S1 reads 'None.' and S2 mentions only aircraft; the first astronaut-specific text is at S3.

The PDF footnote says the scale is 'Based on this measure, but other physical measures are also considered', and that >100 MeV particles are a better indicator of radiation risk to passengers and crews.

The HTML page and the PDF differ in capitalisation and in a few non-biological words (e.g. S2 'Other systems'); 'effects' is the HTML text, 'biological_pdf' the PDF text (whitespace-normalised, footnote marks kept).

Operator wording differs: the PDF column header reads 'Flux level of > 10 MeV particles (ions)', the HTML page reads 'Flux level of >= 10 MeV particles', and SWPC's GOES proton data use '>=10 MeV'. LANDFALL applies each threshold as met-or-exceeded (>=), consistent with the SESC event rule ('greater than or equal to 10 pfu').

data.rule: S level = highest level whose threshold is met (flux >= threshold); below 10 pfu = no S storm

effects.Other systems: Minor impacts on HF radio in the polar regions.

effects.Biological: Passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to elevated radiation risk.
effects.Other systems: Small effects on HF propagation through the polar regions and navigation at polar cap locations possibly affected.

levels.biological_pdf: passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to elevated radiation risk.***

effects.Biological: Radiation hazard avoidance recommended for astronauts on EVA; passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to radiation risk.
effects.Satellite operations: Single-event upsets, noise in imaging systems, and slight reduction of efficiency in solar panel are likely.
effects.Other systems: Degraded HF radio propagation through the polar regions and navigation position errors likely.

levels.biological_pdf: radiation hazard avoidance recommended for astronauts on EVA; passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to radiation risk.***

effects.Biological: Unavoidable radiation hazard to astronauts on EVA; passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to radiation risk.
effects.Satellite operations: May experience memory device problems and noise on imaging systems; star-tracker problems may cause orientation problems, and solar panel efficiency can be degraded.
effects.Other systems: Blackout of HF radio communications through the polar regions and increased navigation errors over several days are likely.

levels.biological_pdf: unavoidable radiation hazard to astronauts on EVA; passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to radiation risk.***

effects.Biological: Unavoidable high radiation hazard to astronauts on EVA (extra-vehicular activity); passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to radiation risk.
effects.Satellite operations: Satellites may be rendered useless, memory impacts can cause loss of control, may cause serious noise in image data, star-trackers may be unable to locate sources; permanent damage to solar panels possible.
effects.Other systems: Complete blackout of HF (high frequency) communications possible through the polar regions, and position errors make navigation operations extremely difficult.

levels.biological_pdf: unavoidable high radiation hazard to astronauts on EVA (extra-vehicular activity); passengers and crew in high-flying aircraft at high latitudes may be exposed to radiation risk. ***

pdf_footnotes: Flux levels are 5 minute averages. Flux in particles·s-1·ster-1·cm-2 Based on this measure, but other physical measures are also considered.
These events can last more than one day.
High energy particle (>100 MeV) are a better indicator of radiation risk to passenger and crews. Pregnant women are particularly susceptible.
